- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., 68.27 → 71.56) — model predicts peak too early and too high.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model fails to recognize when prices are trending down from a high and doesn’t adjust downward enough.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends — model is slow to catch momentum.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility — model overreacts to minor price fluctuations, leading to erratic forecasts.
- Underestimates the persistence of upward trends — model often fails to project sustained price increases after a spike.
- When history shows a strong upward trend, model tends to forecast a peak too soon and then drops too quickly — fails to capture the “slow burn” of price increases.
- Model underestimates the true magnitude of price increases in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon — especially in the last 10 days, true prices often exceed model predictions by 2–5%.
- Model is sensitive to recent history — if the last 5 days are volatile, model overreacts and forecasts extreme values, then corrects too late.
